sentences.zh: 吉娜，我们认为美联储在几个小时内就会提高利率，以降低美国经济中的通胀。

sentences.en: Can you just help us understand the mechanics of that?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我们理解一下其中的机制吗？

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So, as everyone knows, prices are rising really quickly right now on cars, on meat, on couches.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，目前汽车、肉类、沙发等商品的价格上涨得非常快。

sentences.en: And there are a few reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有几个原因。

sentences.en: The government spent a lot of money at the start of the pandemic and throughout last year to sort of blunt the impact of the coronavirus and its effect on workers.
sentences.zh: 政府在疫情初期和去年全年投入了大量资金，旨在减轻新冠病毒及其对工人的影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There were stimulus checks, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，发放了刺激支票。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And that spending fueled really strong demand.
sentences.zh: 而这种支出推动了非常强劲的需求。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, that strong demand collided with supply chains that were all messed up.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这种强劲的需求与陷入混乱的供应链发生了碰撞。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so there were too many dollars chasing too few goods, and inflation really jumped up.
sentences.zh: 因此，太多的美元追逐太少的商品，通胀确实飙升了。

sentences.en: Today, even though the government is spending less, the checks have stopped, the labor market is really strong, and that's helping to sustain this pretty robust demand.
sentences.zh: 今天，尽管政府支出减少了，支票发放也停止了，但劳动力市场依然非常强劲，这有助于维持这种相当稳健的需求。

sentences.en: And it's keeping inflation rising.
sentences.zh: 并且让通胀持续上升。

sentences.en: And so we have this real problem where prices have been going up a lot, and now the Fed is getting worried that inflation is going to get stuck at this higher
sentences.zh: 所以我们面临一个现实问题：价格一直在大幅上涨，现在美联储担心通胀会陷入他们不希望看到的

sentences.en: rate that they do not want.

sentences.en: And so the idea is, if you raise interest rates, if you make it more expensive to borrow money to buy a car or to borrow money to buy a house, then fewer people will do
sentences.zh: 所以他们的想法是，如果你提高利率，如果你让借钱买车或买房的成本变得更高，那么做这些事的人就会减少。

sentences.en: those things.

sentences.en: There will be less demand, and supply will have a chance to catch up, which will allow price increases to slow down a little bit.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 当美联储提高利率时，本质上就像是给经济浇了一大杯冷水。

sentences.en: When the Fed raises the interest rate, it essentially pours a tall glass of cold water on the economy.

sentences.en: It deliberately tries to slow down spending.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 你减缓经济活动是为了控制通胀。

sentences.en: You slow things down to bring inflation under control.
sentences.zh: 这让我一直觉得有点奇怪，因为你描述的是我们自己的政府为了最终帮助经济而损害经济的过程。

sentences.en: Which has always struck me as kind of strange, because what you're describing is a process of our own government hurting the economy in order to eventually help the economy.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这就是各国央行控制通胀的方式。

sentences.en: And so this is the way that central bankers control inflation everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但在美国，

sentences.en: But here in the
sentences.zh: 央行行长们之所以特别关注通胀似乎可能失控的时期，是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: United States, there's a good reason why central bankers tend to be especially attuned to periods where it seems like inflation might hop out of control.
sentences.zh: 因为有一个历史先例，当时他们对通胀反应不够迅速，导致通胀变得非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And that is because there's a historical example where they did not react quickly enough to inflation, where inflation became really painful.
sentences.zh: 这段时期简直是央行行长们的噩梦。

sentences.en: And it's this period that kind of haunts the nightmares of central bankers.
sentences.zh: 那么，请给我们讲讲那段让经济学家们心有余悸的时期。

sentences.en: So tell us the story of that time period that haunts economists.
sentences.zh: 它是从什么时候开始的？

sentences.en: When did it start?
sentences.zh: 故事始于20世纪60年代中后期，也就是林登·B·约翰逊总统任期内，当时政府支出规模巨大。

sentences.en: So the story starts in the mid to late 1960s, really during Lyndon B.
sentences.zh: 本届政府在此时此地，向美国的贫困宣战，不设任何条件。

sentences.en: Johnson's presidency, when there is just this huge amount of government spending happening.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊以试图通过一项名为“伟大社会”的雄心勃勃的计划来解决贫困问题而闻名。

sentences.en: This administration today, here and now, declares unconditional war on poverty in America.
sentences.zh: 我们进行更精准打击的主要武器将是更好的学校、更好的医疗、更好的住房、

sentences.zh: 更好的培训和更好的就业机会，以帮助更多美国人摆脱贫困和苦难。

sentences.en: Our chief weapons in a more pinpointed attack will be better school and better health and better homes
sentences.zh: 而在这一切发生的同时，国家还卷入了越南战争。

sentences.en: and better training and better job opportunities to help more Americans escape from squalor and misery.
sentences.zh: 我已经告诉美国人民，我们将向越南派遣完成任务所需的部队。

sentences.en: And while that's happening, the country's still engaged in the war in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 这也使政府支出增加了数十亿又数十亿美元。

sentences.en: I have told the American people that we would send to Vietnam those forces that are required to accomplish our mission there.
sentences.zh: 本财年为25亿美元。

sentences.en: And that's also increasing government spending by billions and billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 下一财年为26亿美元。

sentences.en: Two and a half billion dollars in this fiscal year.
sentences.zh: 因此，大量的政府资金涌入经济。

sentences.en: And two billion six hundred million in the next fiscal year.
sentences.zh: 通胀开始逐年缓慢攀升。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of government money pouring into the economy.
sentences.zh: 许多经济学家认为，20世纪60年代的政府支出助推了这一进程。

sentences.en: And inflation just starts to gradually ratchet up year after year.
sentences.zh: 但随后通胀持续上升。

sentences.en: And many economists think that the government spending from the 1960s helped to kick off that process.
sentences.zh: 螺旋式上升的通胀现在似乎成了美国经济的固定特征。

sentences.en: But then inflation keeps on rising.
sentences.zh: 它给美国梦蒙上了阴影，让人们难以实现每年都变得更好的愿望。

sentences.en: Spiraling inflation now appears to be a fixture in the American economy.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪70年代，这种螺旋式通胀对美国人产生了另一个重要影响。

sentences.en: And it's casting a shadow on the American dream of doing better and better every year.
sentences.zh: 全国上下形成了一种通胀心理。

sentences.en: By the 1970s, this spiraling inflation had another important effect on Americans.
sentences.zh: 卖家要价高于所需，希望以此覆盖肯定会到来的成本上涨。

sentences.en: The nation was developing a psychology of inflation.
sentences.zh: 而买家现在就买，因为以后价格只会更糟。

sentences.en: The seller asks more than he needs, hoping to cover the cost increase that's sure to come.
sentences.zh: 人们开始改变对金钱的看法，改变对通胀的看法。

sentences.en: And the buyer buys now because the price will only get worse later.
sentences.zh: 为什么现在人们不存钱了？

sentences.en: People began to change the way they thought about their money, the way they thought about inflation.
sentences.zh: 心理是这样的：明天一切都会更贵。

sentences.en: Why aren't people saving these days?
sentences.zh: 这是一种通胀心理。

sentences.en: The psychology is, well, tomorrow everything is going to cost me more.
sentences.zh: 我最好现在就买，管他什么储蓄。

sentences.en: It's an inflation psychology.
sentences.zh: 所以美国人开始觉得他们的钱不值钱了，因为价格太高了。

sentences.en: I better buy now and the heck we're saving.
sentences.zh: 他们开始要求更高的工资来支付不断上涨的开支。

sentences.en: So Americans began to feel like their money wasn't going to go as far because prices were so high.
sentences.zh: 你看到的是，随着公司不得不支付更多工资，他们开始提高价格以覆盖成本。

sentences.en: And they began to ask for higher wages to cover their rising expenses.
sentences.zh: 我们最终陷入了一种价格和工资螺旋式上升的局面，它们在相互追逐。

sentences.en: And you saw that as companies had to pay more, they started charging more to cover their costs.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续到20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: And we ended up in a situation where prices and wages were in this upward spiral and they were kind of chasing each other.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到了同比价格的飞速上涨。

sentences.en: And so that proceeds through the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 值得花点时间来理解那种高通胀到底是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And we're really seeing these very, very rapid price increases on a year-over-year basis.
sentences.zh: 食品杂货是一个很好的例子，因为它们波动很大，但在70年代有时通胀率达到了两位数。

sentences.en: It's worth pausing just a moment to understand what high inflation like that actually feels like.

sentences.en: Wow.

sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，无论是在70年代初还是在79年，都发生了石油禁运。

sentences.en: And during the 1970s, both in the early 70s and then in 79, there were oil embargoes.

sentences.en: The energy crisis is killing them.

sentences.en: And so when those happened, they sort of supercharged this already very high inflation and pushed the cost of gas up quite a lot.

sentences.en: And so, you know, between gas and food and all of these sort of day-to-day necessities, you just saw a wide variety of consumer goods starting to become more expensive.
sentences.zh: 美国人对所有这些通胀有什么感觉？

sentences.zh: 你在价格牌上就能看到，这成了人们日常生活的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Americans did not feel good about all of this inflation, especially in the 1970s when it started really hitting oil prices because they are just so visible.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对此感到愤怒。

sentences.zh: 明确的含义是，他将支持一项在卡特任期内损害经济的政策，而且他不会

sentences.en: And he wants the Fed to take a harder line approach.
sentences.zh: 继续允许通胀像过去那样失控。

sentences.en: So Volcker gets to his Oval Office interview and basically tells Jimmy Carter that if he gets the job, he's going to push interest rates higher.
sentences.zh: 所以他面试后回家，绝对肯定自己得不到这份工作，鉴于他刚才对总统说的话。

sentences.en: And the clear implication there is that he's going to support a policy that hurts the economy while Carter is still in office, and that he's not going
sentences.zh: 没错，因为他刚告诉总统，我会让你变得不受欢迎。

sentences.en: to continue to allow inflation to just run out of control the way it's been doing.
sentences.zh: 正是如此，正是如此。

sentences.en: And so he goes home from this interview, absolutely positive that he's not going to get the job, given what he's just told the president.
sentences.zh: 所以当第二天清晨电话铃响时，他惊呆了。

sentences.en: Right, because he's just told the president, I'm going to make you unpopular.
sentences.zh: 他还在床上，电话是吉米·卡特打来的。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 卡特告诉他，嘿，你得到这份工作了。

sentences.en: And so he's flabbergasted when the next morning, his phone rings very early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 突然间，保罗·沃尔克发现自己成了美联储主席。

sentences.en: He's still in bed, and it's Jimmy Carter.
sentences.zh: 现在，我的论点可以用几句话总结。

sentences.en: And Carter tells him, hey, you got the job.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们需要降低通胀并恢复价格稳定。

sentences.en: And suddenly, Paul Volcker finds himself chairman of the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做不仅是为了通胀本身，还因为对货币缺乏信心与生产性、增长型的经济是不相容的。

sentences.en: Now, my thesis can be summed up in just a few sentences.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅要为了通胀本身而做，还要因为对货币缺乏信心与生产性、增长型的经济是不相容的。

sentences.en: First, we need to bring inflation down and restore price stability.
sentences.zh: 我们需要这样做，不仅是为了通胀本身，还因为对货币缺乏信心与生产性、增长型的经济是不相容的。

sentences.en: We need to do it not just for its own sake, but because lack of confidence in our currency is incompatible with a productive, growing economy.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做不仅是为了通胀本身，还因为对货币缺乏信心与生产性、增长型的经济是不相容的。

sentences.en: We need to build on the consensus that inflation is at the core of our economic problem, that it is public enemy number one.
sentences.zh: 我们需要建立共识，即通货膨胀是我们经济问题的核心，是头号公敌。

sentences.en: We need to resist temptation.
sentences.zh: 我们需要抵制诱惑。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，

sentences.en: Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 而且无需绑定信用卡，那会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.zh: 当你首次下载

sentences.en: New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 这一个月你可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约

sentences.en: New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Gina, once Paul Volcker is the head of the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 那么吉娜，保罗·沃尔克担任美联储主席后，

sentences.en: What does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: So Paul Volcker basically makes good on what he has promised President Jimmy Carter, which is he wages a war on inflation.
sentences.zh: 保罗·沃尔克基本上兑现了他对吉米·卡特总统的承诺，那就是向通货膨胀宣战。

sentences.en: And we really see that start in earnest in October 1979.
sentences.zh: 我们确实在1979年10月看到了这一行动的正式开始。

sentences.en: There's this super dramatic scene on a Saturday night.
sentences.zh: 那是一个周六晚上，场面非常戏剧化。

sentences.en: Paul Volcker decides to hold a press conference, which at the time is very rare.
sentences.zh: 保罗·沃尔克决定召开新闻发布会，这在当时非常罕见。

sentences.en: The Fed doesn't do a lot of these.
sentences.zh: 美联储很少这样做。

sentences.en: And on a Saturday night.
sentences.zh: 而且是在周六晚上。

sentences.en: And on a Saturday night, right?
sentences.zh: 而且是在周六晚上，对吧？

sentences.en: And not just any Saturday night.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是普通的周六晚上。

sentences.en: On a
sentences.zh: 是在

sentences.en: Saturday night when the Pope is in town.
sentences.zh: 教皇访问期间的周六晚上。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so the Washington Press Corps is very, you know, devoted to following the Pope around.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的新闻界当时非常热衷于跟随教皇报道。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Paul Volcker and his communication staff call up the press and say, no, come on down to the Eccles building.
sentences.zh: 保罗·沃尔克和他的公关团队打电话给媒体，要求他们必须到埃克尔斯大楼来。

sentences.en: And Volcker's spokesperson actually has to convince some of the press to show up to this, including the CBS cameraman, who basically says,
sentences.zh: 沃尔克的发言人甚至不得不说服一些媒体人员出席，包括哥伦比亚广播公司的摄影师，他当时说，

sentences.en: you know, I have limited resources and I'm going to the Pope.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我资源有限，我得去拍教皇。

sentences.en: And the press person says, you know, long after the Pope is gone, you're going to remember what happens tonight.
sentences.zh: 新闻官说，教皇离开很久之后，你还会记得今晚发生的事情。

sentences.en: So a lot of drama, a lot of pomp and circumstance.
sentences.zh: 所以，充满了戏剧性、排场和仪式感。

sentences.en: The press comes down.
sentences.zh: 媒体赶到了现场。

sentences.en: And Volcker basically tells the press that the Fed is going to change how it's setting monetary policy, that they are going to shake up their whole approach.
sentences.zh: 沃尔克告诉媒体，美联储将改变制定货币政策的方式，他们将彻底改革整个方针。

sentences.en: And the whole goal here is really just to vanquish inflation, to bring it down once and for all to really sort of get a handle on this.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的唯一目标就是战胜通货膨胀，将其彻底压下去，真正掌控局面。

sentences.en: This is basically a declaration that things are going to change.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一份宣告，表明一切都将发生改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And how does he do it?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Volcker was really committed to the idea that you had to crush inflation completely to get America out of this self-perpetuating cycle.
sentences.zh: 沃尔克坚定地认为，必须彻底粉碎通货膨胀，才能让美国摆脱这种自我强化的恶性循环。

sentences.en: And so he gets aggressive.
sentences.zh: 于是他采取了激进的手段。

sentences.en: He took an interest rate that was already at 10 percent in 1979 and basically pushed it up to 17.6 percent within like a year.
sentences.zh: 他将1979年已经达到10%的利率，在一年内推高到了17.6%。

sentences.en: By early
1981, his policies push rates up to about 19 percent.
sentences.zh: 初，他的政策将利率推高到了约19%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And soon it's close to 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 很快就接近了20%。

sentences.en: And that's just this incredibly high interest rate and has ratcheted up there in an incredibly short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 这利率高得惊人，而且是在极短的时间内飙升上去的。

sentences.en: And just for a moment, explain what it means for the interest rate to be almost 20 percent in the United States because it's kind of hard to fathom.
sentences.zh: 稍微解释一下，在美国利率接近20%意味着什么，因为这很难想象。

sentences.en: So remember, interest rates very directly translate into how much it costs to buy a house, to borrow to buy a car, or to borrow with a credit card.
sentences.zh: 记住，利率直接决定了买房、贷款买车或使用信用卡借贷的成本。

sentences.en: So let's just take a house, for example.
sentences.zh: 我们以买房为例。

sentences.en: If you buy a $100,000 house and you're going to pay it off in 30 years without any interest on that loan, which isn't realistic, but just for the example,
sentences.zh: 如果你买了一套10万美元的房子，打算在30年内还清，假设贷款没有利息（虽然这不现实，但仅作示例），

sentences.en: your payment's going to be about $300 a month.
sentences.zh: 你每个月的还款额大约是300美元。

sentences.en: Of course, if you're paying a mortgage rate and the interest rate on your loan is 20 percent, so around that 1981 level, your payments would be closer to
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你支付抵押贷款，而贷款利率是20%，也就是1981年左右的水平，你的月供会接近

sentences.en: $1,700 a month.
So that could obviously be prohibitively expensive, especially if you're dragging it out over time.
sentences.zh: 这显然会贵得让人难以承受，尤其是如果你还要长期背负债务的话。

sentences.en: It costs so much to borrow at this stage that you're paying thousands, maybe tens of thousands more than you previously would have just to buy a car, a house, a boat,
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段借钱成本太高了，你买车、买房、买船，

sentences.en: whatever it is that you want to borrow money to buy.
sentences.zh: 或者任何你想借钱买的东西，都要比以前多付几千甚至几万美元。

sentences.en: And so people just stop doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们干脆就不买了。

sentences.en: They just stop spending money on those things.
sentences.zh: 他们停止在这些方面花钱。

sentences.en: And as that happens, America sinks into a recession.
sentences.zh: 随着这种情况发生，美国陷入了衰退。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that recession is really painful.
sentences.zh: 那场衰退真的很痛苦。

sentences.en: How bad?
sentences.zh: 有多严重？

sentences.en: Describe it.
sentences.zh: 描述一下。

sentences.en: Terrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: They came in all shapes and sizes, all ages and all backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 他们来自各行各业，各个年龄段，各种背景。

sentences.en: Almost a thousand of them showed up at City Hall in Soddy Daisy today, lined up from one end of the hall to the other.
sentences.zh: 今天在索迪黛西市政厅，近千人排起了长队，从大厅的一头排到了另一头。

sentences.en: They were all there in response to a Help Wanted ad.
sentences.zh: 他们都是为了响应一份招聘启事而来。

sentences.en: Unemployment rose above 10 percent.
sentences.zh: 失业率上升到了10%以上。

sentences.en: All these people stood in line today and filled out applications at Chattanooga's Employment Security
sentences.zh: 今天，所有这些人都在查塔努加就业保障

sentences.en: Office.
sentences.zh: 办公室排队填表申请工作。

sentences.en: Just no jobs.
sentences.zh: 就是没有工作。

sentences.en: Not here in Chattanooga, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想在查塔努加这里没有。

sentences.en: You know, no jobs here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里没有工作。

sentences.en: The human impact of what Paul Volcker is doing with policy is just palpable at this point.
sentences.zh: 保罗·沃尔克的政策对人类的影响在此时此刻显而易见。

sentences.en: People are out of work.
sentences.zh: 人们失业了。

sentences.en: People are seeing their wage growth absolutely crushed.
sentences.zh: 人们眼睁睁看着自己的工资增长被彻底扼杀。

sentences.en: You've got car lots full of cars that just can't sell.
sentences.zh: 车行里停满了卖不出去的车。

sentences.en: You've got homebuilders who just can't sell houses.
sentences.zh: 建筑商卖不掉房子。

sentences.en: So what you see happening is just this outpouring of anger because people know that interest rates are the thing inflicting so much damage and so much pain throughout the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是人们愤怒的宣泄，因为大家都知道是利率在整个经济中造成了如此巨大的破坏和痛苦。

sentences.en: They know that this is Fed policy driving this terrible recession.
sentences.zh: 他们知道是美联储的政策导致了这场可怕的衰退。

sentences.en: And so people mail two by fours, homebuilders mail two by fours to the
sentences.zh: 于是人们寄送木材，建筑商寄送木材给

sentences.en: Federal Reserve in protest of the houses they can't sell.
sentences.zh: 美联储，抗议他们卖不掉的房子。

sentences.en: The car dealers mail car keys in protest of the cars they can't sell.
sentences.zh: 汽车经销商寄送车钥匙，抗议他们卖不掉的车。

sentences.en: And you see at one point, farmers actually bring tractors and circle the Fed in Washington out of protest, you know, of these very high interest rates and the intense
sentences.zh: 有一次，农民们甚至开着拖拉机包围了华盛顿的美联储，抗议这些极高的利率，以及在这一阶段整个经济中感受到的强烈

sentences.en: pain that is being felt just throughout the entire economy at this stage.
sentences.zh: 痛苦。

sentences.en: But Gina, it almost sounds like the cure was worse than the disease.
sentences.zh: 但吉娜，这听起来就像是药比病还重。

sentences.en: While inflation was bad, people were not losing their jobs or getting priced out of loans for homes and cars the way they were once interest rates soared, right?
sentences.zh: 虽然通货膨胀很糟糕，但人们并没有像利率飙升后那样失去工作或买不起房车，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that is actually a school of thought that it was worse to raise interest rates than it would have been to let the inflation go.
sentences.zh: 确实有一种观点认为，提高利率比任由通货膨胀发展更糟糕。

sentences.en: But most economists will tell you that if inflation would have gone unchecked, it might have gotten worse.
sentences.zh: 但大多数经济学家会告诉你，如果任由通货膨胀失控，情况可能会变得更糟。

sentences.en: And the uncertainty around how much money was going to be worth in the future could have been really harmful for the economy and just for Americans as a whole.
sentences.zh: 而且对于未来货币价值的不确定性，可能对经济和美国整体造成更大的伤害。

sentences.en: So how do you plan or save if you don't know what a dollar is going to buy in a year?
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道一年后一美元能买到什么，你该如何规划或储蓄呢？

sentences.en: And so it just wouldn't have been a solid foundation to use to build up the rest of the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以，那将无法为重建经济的其他部分提供坚实的基础。

sentences.en: And Volcker was very, very aware of how painful this all was.
sentences.zh: 沃尔克非常清楚这一切有多痛苦。

sentences.en: And we know now that he really agonized over what he was doing to the economy during this period.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，在那段时期，他对自己给经济造成的伤害感到非常痛苦。

sentences.en: In his memoir, he describes this patch of carpet in his office that he literally wore out from pacing it so much.
sentences.zh: 在他的回忆录中，他描述了办公室里的一块地毯，因为他来回踱步太多，竟然被他磨穿了。

sentences.en: And he heard a lot of feedback.
sentences.zh: 他也听到了很多反馈。

sentences.en: You know, people publicly blamed him for just about everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们公开指责他几乎所有的事情。

sentences.en: There are those who claim Paul Volcker is the real father of this recession.
sentences.zh: 有人声称保罗·沃尔克是这场衰退的真正始作俑者。

sentences.en: Mr. Volcker, welcome.
sentences.zh: 沃尔克先生，欢迎您。

sentences.en: First, are you willing to accept parenthood for this recession?
sentences.zh: 首先，您愿意承认自己是这场衰退的始作俑者吗？

sentences.en: No, I'll claim no paternity.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会认领这个“父亲”的身份。

sentences.en: I don't even like the question being asked that way.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不喜欢这种提问方式。

sentences.en: But he didn't stand down.
sentences.zh: 但他没有退缩。

sentences.en: There's this moment that's pretty well known in the nerdy circles that I run in, when he was prodded on a show called The McNeil-Larer Report.
sentences.zh: 在我所处的专业圈子里，有一个很有名的时刻，当时他在《麦克尼尔-莱勒报道》节目中受到质询。

sentences.en: Let's not forget that while people are concerned about a recession right now, and that's understandable, we have had and still do have a problem of inflation.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，虽然人们现在担心衰退，这是可以理解的，但我们过去有，现在依然有通货膨胀的问题。

sentences.en: And as I suggested earlier,
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，

sentences.en: if we fail to deal with that inflation in a constructive way, I think we can look forward to a lot more economic instability.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不能以建设性的方式处理通货膨胀，我认为我们将面临更多的经济不稳定。

sentences.en: The better job we do on inflation, the better this economy will behave over a period of time.
sentences.zh: 我们在通货膨胀问题上做得越好，经济在一段时间内的表现就会越好。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 对此我毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And Volcker was encouraging the country to basically keep this bigger picture in mind.
sentences.zh: 沃尔克在鼓励全国人民保持这种大局观。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Do you feel that the strategy that you laid out in October to control the money supply is in fact working the way you wanted it to?
sentences.zh: 您是否认为您在十月份制定的控制货币供应量的策略，确实按照您想要的方式在发挥作用？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it's working in the immediate sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，从直接效果来看，它正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: We're more perfectly on track, maybe partly by luck, than one could have imagined.
sentences.zh: 我们走得比任何人想象的都要稳，也许部分归功于运气。

sentences.en: Now, if you look at the economy and you say, are things going in a beautiful way?
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你看看经济，你会说，一切都在向好的方向发展吗？

sentences.en: Obviously, they're not going in such a beautiful way.
sentences.zh: 显然，情况并没有那么美好。

sentences.en: We've had more...
sentences.zh: 我们经历了更多……

sentences.en: I think overall, he is definitely grappling with the pain he's causing the economy, but he is sort of remaining dedicated to this broader goal and this broader plan,
sentences.zh: 我认为总的来说，他肯定在为自己给经济造成的痛苦而挣扎，但他仍然致力于这个更宏大的目标和计划，

sentences.en: which is to bring inflation down, even if it costs a lot to do that.
sentences.zh: 那就是降低通货膨胀，即使为此付出巨大的代价。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And of course, the biggest question of all is, does this work?
sentences.zh: 当然，最重要的问题是，这有效吗？

sentences.en: It is very painful, but it does work.
sentences.zh: 虽然非常痛苦，但确实有效。

sentences.en: We eventually go from 14.6% inflation in March 1980 to closer to 1% inflation by 1986.
sentences.zh: 我们最终从1980年3月的14.6%的通胀率降到了1986年接近1%的水平。

sentences.en: And so you just see this really rapid, really extreme deceleration in price increases.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到了物价上涨速度极其迅速且极端的减缓。

sentences.en: And inflation is under control in a way that it hasn't been in decades.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀得到了几十年来从未有过的控制。

sentences.en: As that happens, you get a lot of really positive knock-on effects throughout the rest of the economy.
sentences.zh: 随着这种情况发生，你会在经济的其他领域看到许多非常积极的连锁反应。

sentences.en: And so consumers start to have much more stable outlooks.
sentences.zh: 消费者开始拥有更稳定的预期。

sentences.en: Businesses also start to feel like they can plan ahead and that they don't have to worry about prices just going crazy.
sentences.zh: 企业也开始觉得他们可以提前规划，不必担心价格会疯狂上涨。

sentences.en: And as those two things happen, we see it really affecting behavior.
sentences.zh: 随着这两件事的发生，我们看到它真正影响了人们的行为。

sentences.en: Lately, American consumers have been shopping with even more vigor than usual.
sentences.zh: 最近，美国消费者的购物热情比以往任何时候都要高涨。

sentences.en: I think everybody's in a good mood by the looks of the mall.
sentences.zh: 我想从商场的情况来看，大家心情都不错。

sentences.en: It looks like it's full of people.
sentences.zh: 看起来到处都是人。

sentences.en: Businesses start to sort of invest again.
sentences.zh: 企业开始重新进行投资。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: economy continues its seemingly inexorable expansion.
sentences.zh: 经济继续其看似不可阻挡的扩张。

sentences.en: Consumers, as interest rates come down alongside inflation, are able to buy houses again.
sentences.zh: 随着利率随通胀下降，消费者又能买房了。

sentences.en: Cars are selling again.
sentences.zh: 汽车销量也回升了。

sentences.en: And today's announcement that personal income shot up at the highest rate in five and a half years comes as the nation's unemployment rate remained near a 30-year low.
sentences.zh: 今天宣布的个人收入以五年半来最快速度增长的消息，正值全国失业率保持在30年来的低点附近。

sentences.en: Really, by the late 1980s and early 1990s, we're having a really strong, solid, steady growth economy.
sentences.zh: 到了80年代末和90年代初，我们确实拥有了一个非常强劲、稳固、持续增长的经济。

sentences.en: A friend of mine told me, try America online.
sentences.zh: 我有个朋友告诉我，试试美国在线。

sentences.en: I said, why?
sentences.zh: 我说，为什么？

sentences.en: I've got a computer.
sentences.zh: 我有电脑。

sentences.en: Then in the 1990s...
sentences.zh: 然后在90年代……

sentences.en: Welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎。

sentences.en: I don't mind saving for retirement anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不再介意为退休储蓄了。

sentences.en: I can research mutual funds, chart all my stocks, and do my banking all from home anytime I want.
sentences.zh: 我可以随时在家研究共同基金、绘制股票图表并处理银行业务。

sentences.en: You get a productivity boom as personal computers come online.
sentences.zh: 随着个人电脑的普及，你迎来了一场生产力繁荣。

sentences.en: And really just we've set the stage for these several decades of very strong, very stable growth.
sentences.zh: 我们确实为随后几十年的强劲、稳定增长奠定了基础。

sentences.en: And that is sort of the legacy of this Volcker era.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上就是沃尔克时代的遗产。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So it's not a stretch to say that Volcker did, as he promised, slay the dragon of inflation with this strategy of higher interest rates.
sentences.zh: 所以说沃尔克信守承诺，通过这种高利率策略成功斩断了通胀这条恶龙，这并不夸张。

sentences.en: And showed that hurting the economy in the short term really does improve the economy in the long term.
sentences.zh: 他也证明了短期内对经济造成阵痛，确实能改善长期的经济状况。

sentences.en: I think that that has become sort of the economic consensus in the time since.
sentences.zh: 我认为这已成为此后经济学界的一种共识。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think people very much attribute the good outcome to Paul Volcker.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们非常认可保罗·沃尔克所带来的良好结果。

sentences.en: So this does great things for Paul Volcker's reputation in the intervening years.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些年来，这极大地提升了保罗·沃尔克的声誉。

sentences.en: And one person who grew up in the inflationary era and who is a real big admirer of Paul Volcker is Jay Powell, the current Fed chair.
sentences.zh: 现任美联储主席杰伊·鲍威尔就是在通胀时代成长起来的，他也是保罗·沃尔克的忠实崇拜者。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And Jay Powell has talked publicly about his deep admiration for Paul Volcker.
sentences.zh: 杰伊·鲍威尔曾公开谈论过他对保罗·沃尔克的深深敬仰。

sentences.en: So when you first became chair, you were seen, you were spotted numerous times carrying
sentences.zh: 所以当你刚出任主席时，人们多次看到你随身携带

sentences.en: Paul Volcker's book under your arm.
sentences.zh: 保罗·沃尔克的书。

sentences.en: When Volcker's autobiography came out a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 那是几年前沃尔克的自传出版的时候。

sentences.en: So I actually thought I should buy, you know, 500 copies of this book and just hand them out at the Fed.
sentences.zh: 我当时甚至想，我应该买个500本，然后在美联储内部发一发。

sentences.en: I didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 我没那么做。

sentences.en: But it's a book I strongly recommend.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一本我强烈推荐的书。

sentences.en: And Hal talked about how he thinks that, you know, he and his colleagues should be thinking about this example as something that they want to emulate.
sentences.zh: 哈尔谈到他认为自己和同事们应该将沃尔克的例子视为效仿的对象。

sentences.en: I don't think there is a, has been a greater public servant in our broad area in our lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们这一生中，我们这个领域里还没有比他更伟大的公仆。

sentences.en: I mean, he really just did exactly what he thought was the right thing all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他总是坚定地做他认为正确的事情。

sentences.en: And he let the chips fall where they may.
sentences.zh: 而且他从不计较后果。

sentences.en: You know, we can all hope to live up to some part of who he is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都希望能活出他的一部分风采。

sentences.en: And so really a long track record of just really looking up to this, this former Fed chair and, you know, his long ago predecessor.
sentences.zh: 所以，他确实长期以来一直仰望着这位前美联储主席，也就是他很久以前的前任。

sentences.en: And if you are somebody like Jay Powell and you study this era closely, as it sounds like
sentences.zh: 如果你是像杰伊·鲍威尔这样的人，并且仔细研究过那个时代，听起来

sentences.en: Powell did, what is the big lesson of the 1970s and Paul Volcker that Powell would carry into a moment like this?
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔确实研究过，那么鲍威尔会从20世纪70年代和保罗·沃尔克身上学到什么重要经验，并带入当下的时刻呢？

sentences.en: I think that the big overarching lesson is that you don't want to let inflation carry on for so long that it becomes sort of a major part of how people think about the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为最核心的经验是，你不能让通胀持续太久，以至于它成为人们看待世界方式的一部分。

sentences.en: Because once that happens, it is so painful to cure.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦发生这种情况，想要治愈它就太痛苦了。

sentences.en: Powell, like many economists in this era, has really studied sort of the pain that Volcker had to put the economy through.
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔和这个时代的许多经济学家一样，深入研究了沃尔克当年不得不让经济承受的痛苦。

sentences.en: And nobody wants to see a repeat of that.
sentences.zh: 没人想看到那种情况重演。

sentences.en: It was a really miserable era.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个悲惨的时代。

sentences.en: And so I think the lesson is you get out ahead of this early.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为经验就是，要尽早采取行动。

sentences.en: You take care of it as soon as it starts to become a problem.
sentences.zh: 一旦问题初现苗头，就要立刻解决。

sentences.en: Basically, you don't be the Fed in the 1960s and 1970s and just let this drag on year after year and kick the can down the road.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你不能像60年代和70年代的美联储那样，让问题年复一年地拖延，把问题留给未来。

sentences.en: You try and take care of it right away.
sentences.zh: 你要尝试立刻解决它。

sentences.en: Right, which is why later today, Powell's going to raise the interest rate just a little,
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是为什么今天晚些时候，鲍威尔会稍微提高一点利率，

sentences.en: which will inflict a little bit of pain, you're saying, so that he never has to do what Volcker
sentences.zh: 你是指这会带来一点点痛苦，这样他就永远不必做沃尔克

sentences.en: did, which is raise it again and again and again and inflict a tremendous amount of pain on the American worker and the American economy.
sentences.zh: 做过的事，即一次又一次地加息，给美国工人和美国经济造成巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Powell is going to nudge the rate up a little bit at this meeting, and he's probably going
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔会在这次会议上小幅上调利率，他可能会

sentences.en: to sort of send a signal that the Fed is going to continue raising interest rates steadily throughout the year.
sentences.zh: 发出一个信号，即美联储将在全年稳步提高利率。

sentences.en: But the goal here is to maybe eventually raise interest rates up to perhaps 3%.
sentences.zh: 但目标是最终将利率提高到3%左右。

sentences.en: So nothing like the 20% that Volcker was touching by the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这与沃尔克在80年代初触及的20%利率完全不同。

sentences.en: So instead of a tall glass of cold water being poured on the economy, it's kind of like a spritz.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不像是一大杯冰水泼在经济上，更像是一点点喷雾。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the sort of hope and dream here is to sort of cool off the economy, to pull down inflation, to get things under control.
sentences.zh: 这里的愿景和梦想是让经济降温，拉低通胀，让局势得到控制。

sentences.en: But to do that quickly and to do that in a gentle way so that you don't have to inflict the tremendous amount of pain that Paul Volcker did in the 1970s and 1980s.
sentences.zh: 但要迅速且温和地做到这一点，这样就不必像保罗·沃尔克在70和80年代那样造成巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: Well, Gina, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，吉娜，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: This has been very enlightening.
sentences.zh: 这非常有启发性。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。
